subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin feels that he has crossed a threshold he didn't notice, becoming bigger and more present.
source_quote: Something hit me, as I surveyed the battlefield. Not literally. Though, given how the last several months have gone, that's worth specifying. No, this was the other kind of thing — the quiet knock inside the chest that means you've crossed some threshold you didn't notice crossing. I've felt it before, in the dark, after bad fights. The body takes stock before the mind does. I was bigger somehow. More there.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin knows it will take the rest of the day to decide how to proceed with his new level-up options because he takes such decisions seriously.
source_quote: I knew immediately how long that was going to take. Not because I couldn't decide, but because I take it seriously, and taking things seriously takes time. Alright, well, that's gonna take the rest of the day.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes that being raised by giants means he doesn’t need ranged abilities because giants toss rocks and his role was to protect them.
source_quote: being a dwarf raised by giants means I don’t have to have any range. Giants toss rocks. Those rocks go far and hurt. My job was to be there and protect the giants from anything that came too close.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recognizes that his habit of saving potions for later is a wrong strategy.
source_quote: I knew it was wrong when I said it. It's always wrong. The potion you don't drink is the potion you die holding.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin admits that saving potions is just how he rolls, despite knowing it's wrong.
source_quote: Wrong strategy, but that's just how I roll.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin understands that the Zhentarim have survived by being willing to do what others won't, and he now understands that better than he would like.
source_quote: The Zhentarim have survived by being willing to do what others won't. I understood that better now than I would have liked.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin acknowledges that he has undergone a dark transition and absorbed lessons from the Underdark that he didn't mean to.
source_quote: I've had what you might call a dark transition. The happy-go-lucky kid who went underground expecting something survivable has spent months watching demon lords and eating mushrooms and coming to understand that the Underdark doesn't care what kind of person you want to be.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz finds pleasure in the moment before making a decision, when possibilities are laid out like a hand of cards.
source_quote: There is a particular kind of pleasure in having options. Not the pleasure of having made the decision — that comes later, and sometimes not at all. The pleasure I mean is the one that arrives in the moment before: the spread of possibilities laid out like a hand of cards, each one representing a different version of how the next fight might go.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes Warcaster is necessary for maintaining concentration on spells like Hypnotic Pattern and Maximilian's Grasp.
source_quote: If I'm maintaining concentration on a spell worth maintaining — Hypnotic Pattern, Maximilian's Grasp — then the ability to hold that concentration when something lands a hit is not decorative. It is the difference between the spell persisting and the spell dissolving at precisely the wrong moment.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz considers Fey Touched valuable because it grants additional prepared spells from the Ebonmire spellbook.
source_quote: Fey Touched was a key, and the Ebonmire spellbook was a door I hadn't fully opened yet. Prepared spells are the real resource for a wizard — not the castings themselves, not the slots, but the selection. What you've loaded before the situation becomes the situation.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz has an instinctive and deeply personal objection to being grabbed.
source_quote: I've been grabbed before. I have an instinctive and deeply personal objection to being grabbed.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz views Telekinetic as a geometry tool for positioning allies rather than just an offensive option.
source_quote: I was beginning to build a picture of Telekinetic not as an offensive tool but as a geometry tool. The Underdark had taught me repeatedly that battles are often decided by who is standing where.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz believes the combination of Fey Touched, Misty Step, and Sculpt Spells forms an interlocking system for battlefield control.
source_quote: The Evoker's toolkit is not a collection of separate spells; it is an interlocking argument about where enemies should be, where allies should be, and which parts of a room I am willing to set on fire.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz writes down Fey Touched with quiet satisfaction after confirming it fits his tactical vision.
source_quote: Fey Touched. That was the one. I wrote it down with the quiet satisfaction of a calculation that checks out.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes that his Darkness spell and Daz’s fire spells have historically conflicted, and they’ve learned to work around it like a bad step in a tunnel.
source_quote: The Darkness spell has always been the problem between Daz and me. He throws fire. I throw shadow. For months we have been apologizing to each other in the aftermath — your spell blocked my line of sight, my darkness ate your targeting — working around it the way you work around a bad step in a tunnel you know well.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir realizes that a grapple can fix the problem of Cloud of Daggers by pinning enemies in place.
source_quote: Cloud of Daggers: a rotating cage of blades, hungry in one fixed point in space. The problem has always been that enemies move. But a grapple — a proper hold, weight-to-weight, the kind that pins something to a specific square of floor — that solved it.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir remembers a monastery lesson on battlefield geometry but cannot recall who taught it or what was said.
source_quote: I had been thinking about it too. [...] There was a class on this. At the monastery. Something about battlefield geometry and the difference between control and proximity. I think it was Brother Heslin — or possibly that was the one who taught falling. I'm genuinely uncertain. Either way, I remember the light through the shuttered window and thinking the form was taking too long. I did not remember what they said.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir understands that using rope to bind a grappled enemy consumes his action but allows him to set up a deadly combo with Daz’s Cloud of Daggers.
source_quote: The grapple could happen in the spare moment before my main action. The binding would consume the action itself. The whole turn — both pieces of it — spent on one enemy, pinned to the floor, with Daz's daggers already spinning above them.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir recognizes that Street Justice allows him to use rope to bind enemies he’s already grappled.
source_quote: I found the Street Justice feat on his behalf — the one that let him use rope to bind enemies he'd already grappled. I watched the recognition arrive in his expression.

subject: Thorin's potential shift to Zhentarim Tactics
fact: Thorin considers adopting Zhentarim Tactics as part of his character story, but the moral implications remain unresolved.
source_quote: That would be a whole change of character for you. Well, I mean, I can work it into my story. I could. It would be honest, even. Not the honesty I prefer — I've always liked honesty you can stand behind without flinching — but there are things you absorb down here whether you mean to or not.

subject: Daz's Ebonmire spellbook
fact: Daz has not fully opened the Ebonmire spellbook, leaving its full potential unresolved.
source_quote: The spellbook we'd taken from Princess Ebonmire had been sitting in my pack like a promissory note I hadn't finished reading.
